stem.text: When concentrated sulfuric acid is added to crystals of sodium bromide, the products include a colourless gas and a brown-coloured substance.
The colourless gas gives a cream precipitate with AgNO<sub>3</sub>(aq).
Which row describes the reactions that produce the colourless gas and the brown-coloured substance?

explanation.text: Two separate reactions happen. First, concentrated sulfuric acid donates a proton to bromide ions: NaBr + H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> → NaHSO<sub>4</sub> + HBr. No oxidation numbers change, so this is an acid–base reaction. Bromide is a strong enough reducing agent that some of the HBr is then oxidised by the sulfuric acid: 2HBr + H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> → Br<sub>2</sub> + SO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O. Bromine goes from –1 to 0 and sulfur from +6 to +4, so this second reaction is redox.
SO<sub>2</sub> is also a colourless gas, but it gives no cream precipitate with AgNO<sub>3</sub>(aq). The cream precipitate (AgBr) identifies the gas meant here as HBr.

optionAnalysis.text: Forming HBr is acid–base, but the brown substance is bromine, which can only form when Br<sup>–</sup> is oxidised. That step is redox.

HBr forms by proton transfer from H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> to Br<sup>–</sup> (acid–base). Bromine forms when HBr is oxidised by H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>, which is reduced to SO<sub>2</sub> (redox).
Swaps the two reactions. No oxidation number changes when HBr forms, and bromine cannot form without electron transfer.
Bromine formation is redox, but HBr forms without any change in oxidation number, so the gas-forming step is acid–base.

reasoningChain: Cream precipitate with AgNO<sub>3</sub>(aq) means AgBr, so the colourless gas releases Br<sup>–</sup> in water: it is HBr.
H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + Br<sup>–</sup> → HSO<sub>4</sub><sup>–</sup> + HBr: oxidation numbers unchanged, so acid–base.
The brown substance is Br<sub>2</sub>: Br goes from –1 to 0, so electrons are lost and this is redox.

inferredMistakes.text: Thinking that any reaction with concentrated sulfuric acid is redox, and choosing D for the HBr step as well.
Taking the colourless gas to be SO<sub>2</sub> (a redox product), which ignores the cream precipitate with AgNO<sub>3</sub>(aq).

bullets: Options C and D were common incorrect answers.

When concentrated sulfuric acid is added to sodium bromide, the colourless gas produced, which gives a cream precipitate with AgNO3(aq), is HBr. This can be deduced because the cream precipitate is AgBr, so the colourless gas must give Br– ions when it dissolves in water. HBr is produced by the reaction H+ + Br– → HBr. This is an acid-base reaction so the correct option must be A or B.

The only brown-coloured product of the reaction between concentrated sulfuric acid and sodium bromide is bromine. Bromine is produced when Br– ions lose electrons. This is a redox reaction, so the correct option is B.
